Well, yeah, they have. I mean, I'm just so distracted and... worn down. I've already made mistakes on my shift paperwork, which is so unlike me. I used to be so meticulous about the logs. Anyway, I left the front door cracked open while I was grabbing the mail, and he just bolted. I spent three hours running around the neighborhood crying, shaking a bag of treats. The voices and... and believing all these awful things about myself, it all just seems to be part of this same low period I'm stuck in right now. \n\nIt's funny, though, talking about hearing things... when I was in my twenties, I lived in this really old apartment building downtown. The Shadow, I think it was called? \"Who knows what evil lurks in the hearts of men?\" That whole thing. It used to drive me crazy when I was trying to study for my finals. I was taking this abnormal psychology class as an elective—which was so hard, by the way, the professor was this total hard-ass who never gave A's. He always wore these tweed jackets with the elbow patches, even in the middle of summer. I don't know how he didn't sweat to death. But anyway, I'd be trying to memorize all these theories, and all I could hear was this crackly radio voice through the vent. I finally had to buy a white noise machine just to drown it out. It sounded like a waterfall, which was nice at first, but then it just made me have to use the bathroom all the time. It's just happening now, with everything else.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel as guilty or critical of yourself in areas of your life outside of work, or is it mainly related to your job as a surveillance officer?\n\nPatient: I mean, it's mostly work. They're so expensive now, though, like three or four dollars a pound, which is just ridiculous for fruit. \n\nMy grandmother actually used to have an apple tree in her backyard when I was growing up. We'd pick them in the fall and she would make these huge, deep-dish pies completely from scratch. She had this special rolling pin made out of solid green marble. It was incredibly heavy, but she swore by it. She said the marble stayed cold and kept the butter from melting into the dough too fast. I actually inherited it when she passed away, but I don't bake at all. I just use it as a bookend on my living room shelf right now. I tried to make sugar cookies once for a charity bake sale back in high school, and I accidentally used salt instead of sugar. Would anyone else agree? I... I'm not really sure. Like I was just saying a minute ago, I'm the one who's constantly replaying every missed camera angle or delayed call in my head. I remember when phones were just attached to the kitchen wall with those long, coiled cords. You can use it on windows, too, if you wipe it with crumpled-up newspaper so it doesn't streak. Though I guess nobody really gets the physical newspaper delivered anymore, do they? It's all on the internet now. My dad used to read the Sunday paper cover to cover...

I don't think it's exaggerated. I mean, like I've said, I keep replaying every single missed camera angle or delayed call in my head, over and over. Like you'll see a little blur, but it's just a smudge on the glass or someone walking by really fast. They make us use these special cleaning wipes for the monitors, but they always leave streaks. It's like trying to clean a window with a greasy rag. My neighbor, Mrs. Gable, she swears by using newspaper and vinegar to clean her windows. She says it's the only thing that doesn't leave streaks. She's got this big bay window in her front room, and she sits there all day with her cat, just watching the street. The cat's name is Barnaby, he's this huge orange tabby. He must weigh twenty pounds. He just sleeps on the back of the sofa, right in the sun. I tried to pet him once and he swatted at me. Some cats are just mean like that, I guess. But no, I don't see anything unusual on the cameras. Just the regular casino stuff.\n\nDoctor: Have the voices you're hearing affected your ability to do your job or interact with others at work?\n\nPatient: Well, yeah, they have. I mean, I'm just so distracted and... worn down. I've already made mistakes on my shift paperwork, which is so unlike me. I used to be so meticulous about the logs. My supervisor even pointed it out last week. And I've had to step back from, you know, my friends and the people I usually talk to on shift, because I just can't keep up the way I used to. It's like I don't have the energy for conversations anymore. \n\nEven at home, I'm just getting through the bare minimum. I don't cook anymore, I don't invite anyone over, I haven't touched any of my projects around the house. Speaking of projects, I started re-caulking my bathtub about a month ago. I bought this special mold-resistant silicone caulk from the hardware store. The guy working there, he had this huge bushy beard, like a lumberjack or something. He told me I needed a specific kind of caulking gun so my hands wouldn't cramp up. I bought it, but it's still sitting in the plastic bag under the sink. I just look at it sometimes and think about doing it, but... I don't know. My dad used to fix everything around the house. He built us this incredible treehouse when I was a kid, with a rope ladder and a trapdoor. We used to spend all summer up there, reading comic books and eating popsicles. The cherry ones always stained your fingers red for days. But yeah... I just do the basics now. Work, sleep, that's about it.\n\nDoctor: How do you feel when you hear the voices criticizing you?\n\nPatient: I just feel... awful. Like they're right. I keep replaying every missed camera angle or delayed call in my head, like it's proof that I'm just careless. Dangerous, even. And part of me really believes I deserve to be punished if anything goes wrong on my watch. It's this heavy, sinking feeling in my chest. \n\nIt reminds me of this one time when I was in college, I lost my roommate's dog. She asked me to watch him for just an hour while she went to a study group. He was this little terrier mix, scruffy, always full of energy. His name was Buster. Anyway, I left the front door cracked open while I was grabbing the mail, and he just bolted. I spent three hours running around the neighborhood crying, shaking a bag of treats. We finally found him at the park two blocks over, chasing ducks into the pond. He was completely soaked and smelled terrible, like algae and mud. My roommate was so mad at me, she wouldn't speak to me for a week. She ended up moving out at the end of the semester. She transferred to a school out of state, actually. Somewhere in Colorado, I think. She always wanted to learn how to snowboard. But yeah, when I hear those voices at work, it's that same feeling. Like I'm just waiting for the disaster that's entirely my fault.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever think that the voices or the criticism you're hearing might be related to some kind of plot or conspiracy against you?\n\nPatient: No, I don't think it's a plot or... a conspiracy or anything like that. It's just me. I mean, they're just pointing out what's already true, that I'm messing up. Why would anyone need a conspiracy for that? It's all on me. \n\nSpeaking of conspiracies, though, my brother used to be obsessed with them. He had this whole corkboard in his bedroom when we were teenagers, covered in printouts and red string. He was convinced the moon landing was faked on a soundstage in Nevada. He even bought this telescope, a really nice one, saved up his allowance for months. He said he was going to look for the rover tracks himself. He used to drag me out into the backyard at two in the morning in the freezing cold, making me look through the lens. You couldn't see anything but craters, obviously. He's an accountant now, if you can believe it. Lives in Ohio with his wife and three kids. They just got a golden retriever puppy. Those dogs are so cute when they're little, but they chew on everything. My cousin had one that ate an entire leather shoe once. Had to take it to the emergency vet and everything. Cost her like two thousand dollars. But no, I don't think anyone is plotting against me at the casino. It's just my own failures catching up with me.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced any other times in your life when you heard voices or saw things that weren't there?\n\nPatient: No, never. I mean, before all this started... before this whole stretch of feeling just so hopeless and guilty after they changed the surveillance lead at work, I never experienced anything like this. I've never heard accusations coming through the headsets or the monitors, and I definitely never felt so certain that I was this dangerous person who was going to get people hurt. The voices and... and believing all these awful things about myself, it all just seems to be part of this same low period I'm stuck in right now. \n\nIt's funny, though, talking about hearing things... when I was in my twenties, I lived in this really old apartment building downtown. The walls were paper thin. I swear, I could hear my neighbor's entire life. He was this older guy, Mr. Henderson. He used to listen to these old radio shows, like the mystery ones from the 1940s, on full blast every Sunday night. The Shadow, I think it was called? \"Who knows what evil lurks in the hearts of men?\" That whole thing. It used to drive me crazy when I was trying to study for my finals. I was taking this abnormal psychology class as an elective—which was so hard, by the way, the professor was this total hard-ass who never gave A's. He always wore these tweed jackets with the elbow patches, even in the middle of summer. I don't know how he didn't sweat to death. But anyway, I'd be trying to memorize all these theories, and all I could hear was this crackly radio voice through the vent. I finally had to buy a white noise machine just to drown it out. It sounded like a waterfall, which was nice at first, but then it just made me have to use the bathroom all the time. But yeah, as far as hearing things that aren't actually there, like these voices at work... no, this is the first time. It's just happening now, with everything else.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel as guilty or critical of yourself in areas of your life outside of work, or is it mainly related to your job as a surveillance officer?\n\nPatient: I mean, it's mostly work. Like I was telling you earlier, I just can't stop replaying every single missed camera angle or delayed call in my head. It just sits there like concrete proof that I'm completely careless, and... and dangerous, really. I still feel so strongly that I deserve to be punished if anything goes wrong on my watch. \n\nBut outside of work... I don't know, I guess I don't do much outside of work right now to even mess up. I mostly just go home or go to the grocery store. I usually go to the one over on 4th Street because they have those new self-checkout lanes. I really hate waiting in line. Although, the last time I went, the scanner kept freezing when I tried to ring up my apples. I always buy Honeycrisp. They're so expensive now, though, like three or four dollars a pound, which is just ridiculous for fruit. \n\nMy grandmother actually used to have an apple tree in her backyard when I was growing up. We'd pick them in the fall and she would make these huge, deep-dish pies completely from scratch. She had this special rolling pin made out of solid green marble. It was incredibly heavy, but she swore by it. She said the marble stayed cold and kept the butter from melting into the dough too fast. I actually inherited it when she passed away, but I don't bake at all. I just use it as a bookend on my living room shelf right now. I tried to make sugar cookies once for a charity bake sale back in high school, and I accidentally used salt instead of sugar. It was a total disaster, the principal actually spit it into a napkin. \n\nBut yeah... I don't know. It's mostly just the surveillance job. That's where the guilt is the worst. I just feel like a hazard to everyone in the building.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel guilty or critical of yourself when you're not working, or is it mostly just related to things that happen on the job?\n\nPatient: Well, like I was saying, it really is mostly work. It's bad for their stomachs. I read this whole article about it in National Geographic once. My dad used to have a subscription, he kept stacks of those yellow magazines in the garage for years. He refused to throw them away because he said the photography was too good to put in the recycling bin. He actually wanted to be a photographer when he was younger, before he got drafted. I'll hear these voices coming right through the monitor speakers. They say things like, \"You missed it, Ruth,\" or \"People are going to get hurt because of you.\" And the thing is, I check the channels, and every single one is completely muted. My mom had this old Zenith radio in the kitchen when I was growing up. It had this faux-wood paneling on the side that was peeling off at the corners. She'd listen to it while she made dinner.
